title: Casper and the Cover
premise: Sable Ravensworth, a disgraced intelligence analyst, answers a burner phone that rings with the voice of her dead mentor, Casper Vane, who faked his death to expose a trilateral financial laundering scheme called the Cover. Hunted by an assassin named Ilse Brandt and disavowed by every agency she once served, Sable must assemble proof from three countries' archives before Frankfurt markets open and the Cover's architects launder a sovereign-scale fortune into legitimacy. Along the way she learns Casper's voice is partly real, partly a lure — he needs her because only her revoked credentials can unlock the final archive. In the end, Sable chooses justice outside the law: she burns her own identity to broadcast the truth publicly, lets Casper vanish for good, and survives as no one at all.
about_author: R. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former financial-crimes consultant who spent a decade inside compliance departments across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail because they helped build them.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ten years after her dismissal, Sable works nights scrubbing data for a private firm in London. A burner phone arrives in her mail with no return address; it rings, and the voice is Casper Vane, her mentor who died in Prague a decade ago. Emotional beat: dread curdling into hunger.

chapters.title: Rules of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The caller gives her ninety seconds of instructions and a phrase only Casper knew. She verifies the voiceprint against old files and finds it authentic — or perfectly forged. She decides to follow one instruction: go to a locker at King's Cross. Beat: cautious complicity.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Inside the locker: a decade-old dossier on 'the Cover,' a laundering architecture spanning three governments, plus a photo of herself taken yesterday. Someone has been watching her for years. Beat: vertigo — she was never out of the game.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt's POV. A professional assassin reviews a contract on an unnamed analyst in London. She prefers clean work and dislikes loose ends; this file has three. She boards a flight. Beat: cold competence with a flicker of unease.

chapters.title: Three Bounces
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Flashback chapter to her firings from three agencies, each for flagging transactions tied to the Cover. She realizes her career wasn't ruined by error but by accuracy. Beat: grief transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Voice on Line Two
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Casper calls again, evasive about being alive. He claims he faked death to survive long enough to finish what they started. She demands proof; he gives her a Frankfurt account number that shouldn't exist. Beat: trust as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in Riga
chapters.summary: Casper's POV (first time). Revealed alive in Riga, Casper manages the operation remotely, rationing truth to keep Sable moving. He knows Ilse is coming and uses Sable partly as bait. Beat: guilt worn like armor.

chapters.title: Followed Home
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Counter-surveillance confirms she's being tailed by someone good — not police. She runs a tradecraft drill she hasn't used in ten years and loses them barely. Beat: fear sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: The Compliance Officer's Bible
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She decodes the dossier: the Cover routes dirty money through central-bank windows timed to market opens. Next window: Frankfurt, eleven days. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: A Friend With Clearance
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She approaches former colleague Dev Anand, still inside a British agency, trading a favor for a records pull. Dev warns her the Cover has friends everywhere — including whoever signed her dismissals. Beat: loyalty tested.

chapters.title: What Ilse Found in Prague
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. En route, Ilse revisits the Prague job she believes she botched — Casper's 'death.' Doubt surfaces: her employers may have orchestrated it and burned her reputation as cover. Beat: the hunter begins hunting her handlers.

chapters.title: Brussels Break-In
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She burgles an EU audit annex for a ledger fragment confirming the Cover's first layer. It nearly works; she leaves a trace she doesn't see. Beat: competence shadowed by hubris.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Her Out
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She confronts Aldous Reeve, the official who dismissed her, now comfortably retired. He denies everything until she quotes the Cover's internal phrase; then he begs her to stop. Beat: power inverted, menace exchanged.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper reveals to his small team that the plan requires Sable's revoked credentials to open a sealed archive in Frankfurt. He omits that the archive may also incriminate him. Beat: the mentor's moral rot exposed to readers.

chapters.title: Dev's Answer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Dev delivers partial records and a warning: his queries triggered an alert. He gives her forty-eight hours' head start and effectively ends his career. Beat: sacrifice freely given.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse intercepts and kills a Cover fixer sent to tidy her up, confirming her suspicion. She now holds a phone number belonging to Casper's network. Beat: alliance of convenience forming in her mind.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hiding in a Rotterdam safehouse, Sable and Casper speak frankly for the first time. He admits using her; she admits needing the truth more than safety. Beat: wounded honesty between two survivors.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cross-referencing names in the dossier, she finds the Cover's architect: a faceless consortium figure called 'the Underwriter.' Every trail dead-ends at a shell with her own dismissal order attached. Beat: personal stakes fully revealed.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Interleaved countdown: Sable plans, Casper maneuvers, Ilse closes in, the Underwriter's network notices the leaks. Beat: converging vectors, rising tempo.

chapters.title: Train to Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable travels by rail under a forged identity, rehearsing the archive breach. A Cover watcher boards at Cologne; she improvises an escape at the platform. Beat: loneliness of the hunted.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Bank
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She cases the Frankfurt depository where the sealed archive lives, discovering her credentials were never revoked — merely suspended, a trap waiting years for her to spring it. Beat: realization that she was always the key.

chapters.title: Ilse Makes a Call
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse contacts Casper directly: she'll trade the Underwriter's location for the truth of Prague. Casper stalls. Beat: three-way chess, no honest players.

chapters.title: Five Days
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable finds evidence Casper helped design parts of the Cover before turning whistleblower. Her faith cracks. Beat: betrayal within betrayal.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Line
chapters.summary: Sable and Casper, phone POV alternating. She accuses him; he confesses partially — he built a door into the machine, then needed someone uncorrupted to walk through it. Beat: fury, then grim partnership.

chapters.title: Reeve's Last Meeting
chapters.summary: Aldous Reeve's POV. Reeve meets the Underwriter's emissary, offering Sable in exchange for protection. He records it himself — insurance. Beat: cowardice with a survival instinct.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable recruits Dev remotely and an exiled auditor, Mara, to help authenticate the archive. The team is three people against three governments. Beat: improbable hope.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs Both Ways
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable uses her suspended credentials at the depository's outer ring as a decoy, drawing Cover security while mapping inner defenses. It works — too well; they now know she's in Frankfurt. Beat: audacity priced in exposure.

chapters.title: Ilse in the Crowd
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reaches Frankfurt, tracks Sable, and instead of killing her, leaves a note: 'Prague. Tomorrow. Bring the truth.' Beat: the assassin defects toward the light.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper flies in against his own protocol, unable to stay remote any longer. He carries the last decryption key and his confession. Beat: a man walking toward his reckoning.

chapters.title: Prague, Again
chapters.summary: Sable, Casper, Ilse POV rotation. In a Prague safehouse, the three uneasy allies compare notes: Ilse's Prague contract was ordered by the Underwriter to bury Casper alive in the system; Casper survived by becoming a ghost. Beat: enemies becoming conspirators.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Final plan set: breach the archive overnight, authenticate the ledger, broadcast before Frankfurt opens. Reeve's recording surfaces via Dev, giving them the Underwriter's identity thread. Beat: resolve hardened by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Breach
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Night infiltration of the depository. Alarms, locked doors, her suspended credentials finally accepted at the inner vault. She holds the master ledger in her hands as security floods the floor below. Beat: triumph laced with terror.

chapters.title: The Underwriter's Face
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Decrypted, the ledger names the Underwriter: a committee, not a person — including the agency director who fired her and officials in all three governments. No single head to cut off. Beat: despair at systemic evil.

chapters.title: Rooftop Standoff
chapters.summary: Sable and Ilse POV. Cornered on the depository roof, Sable negotiates with Cover security while Ilse covers her escape, wounding her own former employers' men. Beat: loyalty paid in blood.

chapters.title: One Hour to Open
chapters.summary: All POV rotation, rapid cuts. Authentication races the dawn; Casper is intercepted; Dev fights institutional firewalls; Mara verifies hashes; Ilse buys minutes with violence. Beat: full-throttle convergence.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At 9:00 Frankfurt time, the authenticated ledger goes public across exchanges, newsrooms, and three parliaments simultaneously. Trading in implicated instruments halts; the Cover collapses mid-transaction. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: What Casper Owes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper surrenders himself to Ilse rather than flee, asking her to deliver him to prosecutors — his confession completes the record. Beat: redemption purchased with surrender.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Three Governments
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hearings begin; some guilty fall, many maneuver. Sable watches from the crowd, anonymous, her testimony given under a protected identity that erases 'Sable Ravensworth' entirely. Beat: bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: No One at All
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Months later, living under a new name in Lisbon, Sable receives a blank postcard — Casper's signal that he's free and gone. She doesn't answer. Beat: peace chosen over closure.

chapters.title: The Cover, Uncovered
chapters.summary: Epilogue, omniscient-leaning Sable POV. A new analyst somewhere flags an odd transaction and, this time, is believed. The system Sble cracked has learned — slightly. Final beat: vigilance as legacy, the price of survival paid forward.
